title: Understanding the Problem
text: To find the net force, we need to use the work-energy principle. The work done by the net force is equal to the change in kinetic energy of the car.

title: Kinetic Energy Formula
text: The initial kinetic energy of the car can be calculated using the formula: $$KE=\tfrac{1}{2}mv**{2},$$ where $$m$$ is the mass and $$v$$ is the velocity.

title: Convert Speed to $$\tfrac{\text{m}}{\text{s}}$$
text: The initial speed is given in $$\tfrac{\text{km}}{\text{h}}.$$ Convert it to $$\tfrac{\text{m}}{\text{s}}$$ by multiplying by $$\frac{5}{18}$$.

title: Work Done by the Net Force
text: The work done by the net force is equal to the initial kinetic energy, which is also equal to the force times the stopping distance: $$\text{Work}=\text{Force}\times{x}$$.

title: Calculate the Net Force
text: Rearrange the work formula to find the force: $$\text{Force}=\text{Work}/x.$$ Use the initial kinetic energy as the work done.
